_comment: Qwen3.5/3.6 multi-token-prediction head. It ships inside its targets' HF checkpoints (`checkpoint_of`), so it has no configs of its own: under `spec/mtp` it compiles on every selected `qwen3-5-moe` config that declares its layers (`mtp_num_hidden_layers` above zero, the source its `num_hidden_layers` replaces from), that config verbatim. In such a checkpoint its tensors sit under `checkpoint_prefix` (`language_model.mtp.*`, MLX's layout): a target checkpoint holding tensors there carries its head, which loads from the target's own store under the bare names it binds. An MLX conversion that strips the head publishes it apart as a drafter repo named from the target's (`org/X-4bit` → `org/X-MTP-4bit`, `drafter_repo_infix`), whose `model_type` is the identity the head registers under, `qwen3_5_mtp`, and whose tensors are stored bare (`fc.*`, `layers.0.*`, `norm.*`, `pre_fc_norm_*`; hence the empty decoder prefix). It has no embed_tokens / lm_head of its own: the loader lends it the target's. Its decoder layers are the MTP layers, so `num_hidden_layers` REPLACES the backbone's count with `mtp_num_hidden_layers`. Norms as the Qwen3.5 family (zero-centered on HF checkpoints; MLX-affine ones store the full gain, which the norm offset rule reads as-is); the routed experts renormalize top-k as the target's. It DRAFTS OVER A VOCABULARY PREFIX: its logits are the target lm_head's first 65536 rows (`vocab_size`; token ids in BPE merge order, the most frequent first), so a draft costs a quarter of the 248k-row lm_head read; it embeds every token (`embed_vocab_size`). Every emitted token is still the target's choice (a draft is only a proposal it verifies); what the prefix costs is the drafts it cannot make: on the MLX oracle (k=3, code/story/repeat prompts) 2.85 tokens per verify step against 2.94 at the full vocabulary. Halving again does not pay: at k=2 on the bench prompts (the same oracle) 32768 costs 3.9% tokens a step against 65536 — the head's full-vocabulary top-1 leaves the half prefix on about 13% of positions — several times the ~1-2% of a verify cycle the halved lm_head read saves, while 65536 costs 1.5% against the full vocabulary, well under what its 4x smaller read saves. It drafts each sequence of a step as many tokens as keep the step's verify rows — each sequence's token and its drafts — within `spec_verify_rows`, at most `spec_drafts` (`scratchy_serving_engine::spec_decode::DraftBudget`): eight rows, the verify-sized bucket (`METAL_VERIFY_ROWS`; `pick_bucket`: the smallest `bucket_m` at or past the rows), so two drafts at one or two sequences (three and six rows), one at three or four (six and eight), none past four — a verify step past eight rows runs the 64-row prefill-shaped tape, where a verify row costs a prompt row. One request pays on both GPUs measured (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, with drafts vs without: base M5 output tok/s 1.36-1.38x sampled; M5 Max, at this head, TPOT 1.33x on the code prompt and 1.51x on a long one, greedy). Past the gate the head's pass 1 still runs, KV-only (no lm_head, no drafts), so its requests keep their head KV and draft again once the step is back within the gate. Where more rows pay depends on the GPU and on the target (a dense one's rows cost far less). TODO: one budget per device profile and target, derived at expansion from the verify and plain tapes' costs (scratchy_serving_engine::spec_decode::mtp's module docs carry the measurements, with the rest of MTP's open work). Its KV is its target's capacity (a pool mirroring the target's blocks), so its KV codec is decided at the target's layer count (`target_num_hidden_layers`, its config's `num_hidden_layers`): the target's codec, under which it stages through the target's scratch.
